上所施下所效也。从攴从孝。凡教之屬皆从教。

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 字形 / 甲骨部件分析 / 形義通解
evidence.text: The database presents 教’s oracle-bone form as 攴 + 子 + 爻, identifies 爻 as phonetic, and reports the graph’s core sense as teaching. It gives a proposed pictorial interpretation of 攴 as a teaching implement and爻 as materials for teaching counting or divination; this is an interpretation attributed to Shen Pei, not a directly established description of the object. It says some bronze forms use 攴 + 學, and some Warring States bamboo forms use 言. It reports oracle-bone use as a personal or place name, bronze and manuscript use for teaching, and cites manuscript examples for teaching, instruction, and command. Its reading of the later left component as 爻+子 (𡥉), with 孝 as a later graphic corruption, is one source’s analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 教

evidence.field: 《說文》 / 《廣韻》 / 普通話 / 形義通解
evidence.text: The database transcribes the Shuowen account as 敎: ‘上所施下所效也。从攴从𡥉’ and lists ancient forms 𧧿 and 𤕝. It records Guangyun 古肴切 and a second reading elsewhere, 古孝切. It reports Mandarin readings jiāo and jiào. The same entry says identifying 孝 as the sound element is a later corrupted form, contrasting with the Shuowen transcription and later dictionaries that preserve 孝 in the graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 教

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, as quoted in CUHK Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen explanation says: ‘上所施下所效也。从攴从𡥉’—what those above enact, those below imitate; composed of 攴 and 𡥉. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 教

evidence.source: 漢字ペディア, Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation
evidence.text: This dictionary labels 教 a 会意形声 graph, analyzes it as 攴 plus a form read カウ (𡥉; 孝 as an altered form), and explains the composition as compelling someone to learn. It records Japanese on-reading キョウ and kun-readings おしえる・おそわる, with senses including teach/guide and admonition or religious teaching. This is a modern dictionary’s account and conflicts in emphasis with sources that treat 爻 as the phonetic element.
evidence.title: 教 | 漢字ペディア

evidence.source: Kotobank, entry based on 平凡社『普及版 字通』
evidence.field: 字形 / 字訓 / 訓義 / 語系
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone and bronze forms, calls the old form 敎, and analyzes it as 爻 + 子 + 攴. It describes 爻 as a building feature and proposes an ancient school setting, while also noting the Shuowen account connecting the graph with 孝/效 and arguing that 孝 is not graphically related to 爻. It reports oracle-bone divination about gathering nobles’ children for instruction, and glosses 教 as teach, school, and a causative verb. These formation and social-setting explanations are hypotheses in a dictionary entry; the described structures are not independently verified here from glyph images.
evidence.title: 教(キョウ)とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.source: Xin Changhu and Lin Jiabao, article record at Korea Citation Index
evidence.text: The 2022 article (교육철학 82, pp. 109–128) revisits readings of 教 in oracle-bone inscriptions and proposes that the right-hand element may be 父 rather than 攴 in some forms, yielding an interpretation involving rulers’ participation in education. The abstract presents this as a new interpretation, illustrating that readings of the early graph remain disputed; the article’s full argument and glyph evidence were not inspected.
evidence.title: 갑골문(甲骨文)에 나타난 ‘교(敎)’의 자형(字形) 분석과 의미 고찰

evidence.source: Yang Jianzhong, Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics
evidence.text: The article argues that oracle-bone 教 and 學 were distinct graphs and words: 教 meant ‘impart teaching’ and belonged to the 見 initial, while 學 had readings for learning and causing someone to learn. Their later semantic overlap led to graph interchange in bronze inscriptions and some Chu manuscripts. This conflicts with accounts treating 教 and 學 as historically one graph or treating 學 as a source-form, so the proposed identity/derivation should not be asserted as settled.
evidence.title: 杨建忠：说“教”“学”

evidence.field: historical examples in 形義通解
evidence.text: The entry cites a bronze-inscription example from the Zhongshan Wang Ding, 越人修斆備信, interpreted as cultivating education and trust; Warring States manuscript examples include 信陽長臺觀簡 ‘教箸’, 郭店《老子》 ‘行不言之教’, and Shuihudi Qin slips ‘民之既教’ and ‘以教道民’. The cited manuscript and bronze contexts support teaching/instruction uses by those periods. The sources inspected do not establish a complete dated semantic path from the oracle-bone name/place-name uses to each later use, nor independently establish the exact dates of every cited manuscript.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 教

evidence.source: Beijing Municipal Government / National Museum of Classic Books
evidence.text: The museum’s 2026 page describes an oracle-bone inscription ‘其教戍’ and interprets 教 there as transmit/instruct, cause, or command, read jiāo. It says the oracle form is phonosemantic, from 攴 with 爻 as phonetic, and that 子 was later added semantically to foreground children as learners. This differs from the CUHK database’s description of the oracle form as already containing 攴, 子, and 爻; the discrepancy is retained rather than harmonized. The page dates its own publication to 2026, not the inscription.
evidence.title: “教戍”甲骨

evidence.text: The database lists 教 readings jiāo and jiào, Guangyun 古肴切 and 古孝切, with Middle Chinese categories 見母、肴韻、開口二等: level and departing tones respectively. These are host-character readings; they do not establish sound correspondence with any component by themselves.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 教

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows 1626 and 1645 (local; upstream click-through unavailable for this source in this research)
evidence.text: Exact local rows: 教 jiāo | Middle Chinese kaew | Old Chinese *s.[k]ˤraw; 教 jiào | kaewH | *s.kˤraw-s. The 2014 reconstruction table elsewhere inspected for 爻 reports *N-kˤraw, while the dossier’s cited Zhengzhang values are *kraːw for 教 and *ɢraːw for 爻. In Baxter–Sagart, 孝 is *qʰˤ<r>uʔ-s (local row 3809), not a close match to 教. Thus 爻 has the independently supported phonetic role in early forms; the present graph component 孝 is not a convincing Baxter–Sagart phonetic match. Local file evidence is reported as such and is not offered as an external source URL.
evidence.title: 爻 - Wiktionary (Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang comparison inspected; local dataset differs in notation/source row)

evidence.field: Old Chinese / Middle Chinese reconstruction tables
evidence.text: The entry reports 爻 as Mandarin yáo, Middle Chinese hæw, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *N-kˤraw, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *ɢraːw; its table gives 教 *kraːw/*kraːws in Zhengzhang’s phonetic-series list. These values support a historical phonetic association between 爻 and 教 in those reconstruction frameworks. The systems differ in notation and should not be conflated. The page lists possible original interpretations of 爻’s crossed marks (divination stalks, calculation slips, or crossing marks) without resolving the referent or a recoverable original object-name pronunciation; no object-name loan claim is needed for 爻’s phonetic role here.
evidence.title: 爻 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction and current readings
evidence.text: The page reports 孝 as Mandarin xiào, Cantonese haau3, Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese xæwH and Old Chinese *qʰˤ<r>uʔ-s (with a variant notation *qʰˤ<r>uʔ-s also present in the local dataset), and Korean 효 (hyo). This is substantially different from 教’s Baxter–Sagart forms, so the dossier’s simple claim that modern 孝 supplies 教’s sound is not supported by this historical comparison. The graph’s relation to the early component 𡥉/爻+子 is a separate paleographic question.
evidence.title: 孝 - 维基词典

evidence.text: The official Unihan record opened for U+5B5D reports kMandarin xiào, kCantonese haau3, kDefinition ‘filial piety, obedience; mourning’, and kGSR 1168a. evidence.text: The entry analyzes oracle-bone 教 as 攴 + 子 + 爻, with 爻 also serving as the phonetic; its interpretation of 攴 as a teaching implement and the scene of teaching children to count or divine is attributed to Shen Pei. It reports oracle-bone use for personal and place names; bronze use for teaching; and Warring States manuscript examples for teaching, instruction, and command. It says some bronze forms use 攴 + 學 and some Warring States slips use 言; it calls 孝 a later corrupted graph for the left-side 爻+子 form. It quotes Shuowen 敎 as ‘上所施下所效也。从攴从𡥉’ and lists Guangyun 古肴切. evidence.text: This dictionary describes old 教 as 爻 + 子 + 攴 and interprets 爻 as a building feature, proposing an ancient educational setting. It also reports oracle-bone divinations about gathering nobles' children for instruction and records senses including teaching, school, and a causative use. These are dictionary hypotheses and reports, not independently verified inscription readings or a demonstrated semantic chronology. It explicitly objects that 孝 is graphically unrelated to 爻.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
